analysis:
Documentation-only batch. installation.md head 219-256 adds a user-initiated `darkbloom update --rollback` section: the updater retains the signed predecessor in ~/.darkbloom/recovery/predecessor/ (UpdateInstallLayout.snapshotLiveAsPredecessor). Rollback drains, performs a journaled swap, restarts the provider and quarantines the installed release. Only one predecessor is kept. cli-reference.md head 743-769 adds the matching flags. It is changed per file_changes, but that range is not visible in these units. Units 14/15 (head 2123-2545) are unchanged surrounding text: paths, env passthrough and runtime constants. The head 1852/1859-1860 changes are not visible.

Security relevance: this is an operator-initiated downgrade path. It touches T-043, where watchdog rollback authority is the same replaceable binary, and the T-013/T-034/T-054 code-identity contracts. The operator (ADV-001) can already run arbitrary code locally, so a local downgrade grants no new trust. Serving authorization still depends on the coordinator and App Attest qualification and revocation (A-017, TB-011), not on local install state.

Unverified implementation contracts:
- The predecessor directory under the user-writable ~/.darkbloom is re-verified (codesign DR, hashes) before the swap and restart.
- Rollback cannot restore a revoked or unqualified build that the coordinator still admits.
- A quarantined build cannot be suppressed to block security updates. The docs say only the exact version is skipped and a newer release installs normally.
- The interaction with the fan helper and cluster refusal holds.

The docs make no claim of re-verification, and the implementation (UpdateRollback.swift, UpdateInstallLayout.swift) is not supplied. These need source review but are not evidence of a regression. T-043 may need a threat-model note covering the new manual rollback entry point.
